title: Error Corrections and Prior Period Adjustments
learning_objectives: Calculate impact on prior period retained earnings
Distinguish errors from changes in estimates

content.definition: Errors are mistakes in recognition, measurement, presentation, or disclosure in previously issued financial statements

errors_vs_changes.error: Mistake in prior period - RESTATE prior periods
errors_vs_changes.change_in_estimate: New information, not a mistake - PROSPECTIVE, no restatement
errors_vs_changes.change_in_principle: Change in accounting method - RETROSPECTIVE application (not an error)

correction_method.retrospective_restatement: Correct prior period financial statements as if error never occurred
correction_method.retained_earnings_adjustment: Adjust beginning retained earnings of earliest period presented for cumulative effect
correction_method.disclosure: Describe error and impact on prior periods

inventory_errors.effect: Impacts COGS, net income, and retained earnings
inventory_errors.self_correcting: Yes - corrects itself over two years if not corrected
inventory_errors.example: Ending inventory overstated: COGS understated, NI overstated. Next year: Beginning inventory overstated, COGS overstated, NI understated.

accrual_errors.example: Failed to record accrued expense → Expenses understated, NI overstated
accrual_errors.correction: Increase expense (decrease NI) in error year, adjust RE

depreciation_errors.example: Failed to record depreciation → Expense understated, asset overstated
depreciation_errors.correction: Record depreciation for all omitted periods, adjust RE

revenue_recognition_errors.example: Recorded revenue too early or too late
revenue_recognition_errors.correction: Adjust revenue and RE for all affected periods

calculation_example.error: Year 1 ending inventory overstated by $10K. Tax rate 30%. Discovered in Year 3.
impact_year_2: Retained earnings Year 2 end: No net effect (error self-corrected)
calculation_example.correction_entry_year_3: If discovered before Year 2 closed: Adjust Year 1 RE and inventory. If discovered after Year 2 closed: No entry needed if preparing Year 3 statements (error self-corrected by end of Year 2).

journal_entry_patterns.error_overstated_revenue: DR Revenue (or DR Retained Earnings if prior period), CR Receivable/Liability
journal_entry_patterns.error_understated_expense: DR Expense (or DR Retained Earnings if prior period), CR Payable/Asset

counterbalancing_errors.definition: Errors that self-correct over two accounting periods
examples: Accrual errors (if properly recorded next period)
counterbalancing_errors.note: Even though self-correcting, must restate if discovered before self-correction completes

examples: Capitalization vs. expense errors (capitalize when should expense, or vice versa)
non_counterbalancing_errors.note: Require correction entry regardless of when discovered

cpa_exam_tips: Errors = Restate prior periods. Changes in estimates = Prospective.
Inventory errors self-correct over 2 years but must restate if discovered
Adjust beginning RE of earliest period presented for cumulative effect
Tax effect: Error adjustment is after-tax amount
Formula: If overstated asset/revenue or understated liability/expense → overstated NI and RE

key_points: Adjust beginning retained earnings for cumulative effect
Changes in estimates ≠ errors (estimates are prospective)
